scores.rationale: The plan is a component catalog with no phases or build ordering, so nothing is sequenced from the substrate upward.
No Phase 0 or thin end-to-end production slice is defined; the plan describes the whole system at once.

scores.evidence: Option A: Shared DB, schema per tenant / Option B: Shared DB, tenant_id in all tables / Option C: Dedicated DB per tenant (costly)
scores.rationale: Tenancy options are listed, but there is no default, no flip condition, and other irreversible choices (Kafka vs RabbitMQ, currency) are left silent.
No within-phase ordering by blast radius exists.

scores.evidence: ✓ Row-level security: tenant_id in every query
scores.rationale: Security has a standalone section with a checklist and tenant middleware, but it isn't tied to phases, and the checklist is partly label-only.
Metrics and alerts are described in a standalone section, not from a first phase, and are mostly business KPIs.
There is no mention of reproducible builds, IaC, environments, or seeded data.
Retries, idempotency keys, dead-letter queues and Multi-AZ appear, but they are scattered and not threaded by phase.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, although it adds none.
There is no explicit list of deferred work or pull-forward conditions; the tenant migration section is only a scaling procedure.

note: This is a broad component-level design document with no phases, walking skeleton, or deferral logic, so it scores low on the rubric despite reasonable technical content.
